Only after the last active actor link closes does the existing finalizeEnd claim source-removed/zero-hit-points and append one terminal ended event. Removing the actor link before finalization means normal remove cleanup does not remove that corpse. All three new callers run within existing mutation transactions; there is no parallel ending or refund path. Repeated zero/dead updates emit no duplicate events. Reverse death order with a suppressed effect also preserves the surviving link and ends once on the last death.

S2 NON-MATERIAL — No missed applicable zero-HP/death seam established. The independent probe matrix covers update_combatant damage, set_suffocation drop, explicit instant death with HP still above zero, exhaustion level-6 death, exhaustion clamping to zero, and nonlethal unconscious-at-zero damage, each with one/two swarms. Closure follows HP zero OR dead, so it does not incorrectly require the status to be dead. adjust_hp is character-only; encounter combatants have no character identity kind, and targeting the swarm with adjust_hp is refused. A player-character-rules swarm that is dying rather than dead is not an admitted Pipes binding: start_effect refuses a creature already using those rules under its derived remove cleanup, and update_combatant refuses opting an owned swarm into those rules. Both admission orders were probed. resolveCombatantDeathSave therefore supplies no missing reachable Pipes transition. Checkpoint materialization/restoration at partial death preserves the recorded flag, removed/surviving links, events and redeemed credit. Restoring both pre-death and partial-death replay snapshots and replaying the same zero-HP writes yields byte-identical canonical replay rows, in combat and after combat closure.

Independently rerunning with origin/main records confirms that refusal and zero issued credits.
